# Hospital Energy Insights

> Free tools and guides for NHS trusts, health boards, ambulance trusts and independent hospitals in England, Scotland and Wales: a half-hourly (HH) electricity analyser (base load, day and night use, out-of-hours use in clinics and offices, peaks against agreed supply capacity and headroom for heat pumps, EV charging and CHP removal, unusual days, solar self-consumption, PDF and Excel reports), a solar PV calculator fed by the measured profile, and sourced guides to net zero targets, funding, heat decarbonisation, moving away from gas CHP, electrical capacity, solar and energy efficiency on healthcare estates.

Independent: not part of, or endorsed by, the NHS.

Operated by Kinetic Energy Consulting. Free to use, no sign-up. The analyser runs entirely in the browser: meter data is never uploaded.

Scope: healthcare estates, NHS and independent sector. Results are indicative estimates from the data loaded: costs are energy cost at the rates entered, not guaranteed savings, and whole-site data shows when energy is used, not which equipment uses it. The method is set out on the How it works page.

Method in brief: base load is the 5th percentile of valid half-hourly demand; out-of-hours (closed-hours) excess is energy used outside the opening hours above that base load; missing readings are left out, never counted as zero; annual figures are scaled from valid hours and withheld under 180 days of data; kVA is kW divided by an assumed power factor.

## Tools

- [Analyser](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/analyser/): the half-hourly analyser, in the browser.
- [Solar calculator](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/solar-calculator): solar PV sizing, cost, payback and PPA comparison over 25 years; opens with the analyser's measured share of output used on site.

## Core pages

- [Hospital Energy Insights: HH data, solar and net zero tools](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/): Free half-hourly analyser and solar calculator for NHS and independent healthcare estates: upload HH data, see base load, peaks and heat pump headroom, size solar from the measured profile, download reports; analysis runs in the browser.
- [How the hospital energy analyser works](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/how-it-works): The method in full: reading files, data checks, opening hours (hospital 24-7 preset), base load (5th percentile), closed-hours excess, costs, annualisation, findings, capacity and headroom, solar hand-off, and limits.
- [Questions about Hospital Energy Insights](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/faq): Who it is for, not an NHS tool, 24-hour sites, information governance, the solar hand-off, heat pumps, gas, cost, privacy and what the results mean.
- [Contact](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/contact): Enquiries to Kinetic Energy Consulting, which runs the site.
- [Sample hospital electricity report from HH data](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/sample-report): A sample report for a made-up community hospital: 1.35 GWh a year, 63% base load, a September base load step worth about £31,000 a year, 76% of a 400 kVA supply at peak, room for a 100 kW heat pump, and 99.8% of solar used on site at 299 kWp.
- [About Hospital Energy Insights and Paul Johnston](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/about): Who runs the site (Kinetic Energy Consulting, Managing Director Paul Johnston), why the analyser is free, and how the guides are sourced and checked.
- [Hospital solar sizing from half-hourly data](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/solar): Sizing solar for hospitals from half-hourly data: why share used on site decides value, a worked community hospital example (99.8% used at 299 kWp, 54% at 1,196 kWp), and how the analyser passes the figure to the solar calculator.

## Guides

- [How NHS sites get half-hourly electricity data](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/get-your-data): Who holds half-hourly data, what to ask your supplier for, the file layouts the analyser reads, and what to do if your supplier cannot provide it.
- [Decarbonising healthcare estates: where to start](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/healthcare-estates-decarbonisation): The decarbonisation challenge for healthcare estates: gas heat is the biggest source; targets, PSDS ending, grid capacity, 24/7 operation and falling grid carbon; a six-step order of work starting with half-hourly data.
- [NHS net zero targets in England, Scotland and Wales](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/nhs-net-zero-targets): NHS England net zero 2040 (direct) and 2045 (supply chain); NHS Scotland net zero 2040, renewable heat in NHS-owned buildings by 2038, buildings minus 75%; NHS Wales 16% by 2025 and 34% by 2030, no new fossil CHP and all decommissioned by 2035; supplier carbon reduction plans; IHPN 2035.
- [NHS decarbonisation funding in 2026: what is left](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/decarbonisation-funding): Healthcare decarbonisation funding: PSDS no new commitments (Phase 4 to March 2028, £510/tCO2e cap); GBE £100m NHS solar (2025), 162 sites done and £25m for 40 more (May 2026); £74m for 82 trusts (Feb 2026); Scotland Public Sector Heat Decarbonisation Fund; Wales Invest to Save; PPAs and EPCs.
- [Hospital heat decarbonisation: heat pumps and steam](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/heat-decarbonisation): Hospital heat decarbonisation: heat decarbonisation plans (whole building approach, electrical capacity section), lowering flow temperatures, steam to point-of-use, hot water safety under HTM 04-01, heat recovery from cooling, heat network zoning, and the electrical load (1 MW heat at efficiency 2.5 needs about 400 kW).
- [Moving away from gas CHP in hospitals](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/moving-away-from-chp): Gas CHP versus grid in 2026: gas 0.182 and grid 0.131 kgCO2e/kWh; with 35%/45% CHP efficiencies, CHP 0.182 kg vs grid plus boiler 0.137 kg vs grid plus heat pump 0.069 kg per kWh of gas; NHS Wales decommission fossil CHP by 2035; removing CHP raises grid import by its output (1 MW is about 1,050 kVA).
- [Hospital electrical capacity for heat pumps and EVs](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/hospital-electrical-capacity): Hospital electrical headroom: agreed supply capacity (kVA) minus winter peak (kW/power factor); test heat pump input (1 MW heat at efficiency 2.5 is about 400 kW), CHP removal (1 MW is about 1,050 kVA) and EV charging; options if short; resilience and HTM 06-01.
- [Solar for NHS trusts, health boards and private hospitals](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/solar-on-healthcare-estates): Solar on healthcare estates: 24/7 hospitals use 90%+ of a well-sized system, clinics 55 to 80%; measure share used on site in the analyser and pass it to the solar calculator; roofs, car park canopies, ground mounts, helipad glare; G99 and resilience; GBE NHS solar funding and PPAs.
- [Hospital energy efficiency: where the quick wins are](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/hospital-energy-efficiency): Hospital energy efficiency: theatre ventilation setback (HTM 03-01, NHS Estates Technical Bulletin 2026/1), BMS schedules for non-clinical areas, LED with controls, steam traps and insulation, variable speed drives, base load steps, and proving savings with half-hourly data.
- [ERIC, EFPMS and benchmarking NHS estates energy](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/estates-returns-and-benchmarking): NHS estates reporting: ERIC (England, mandatory, £14.4bn estate running cost 2025/26, acute EUI about 211 kWh/m² in 2024/25), EFPMS (Wales, includes CHP), Scottish board sustainability reports; comparing fairly; what half-hourly data adds.
- [Worked example: a year of HH data from a hospital](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/example-hospital-analysis): A made-up community hospital run through the analyser: 1.35 GWh a year, 63% base load, a 22 kW ventilation setback fault from September worth about £31,000 a year, a 100 kW heat pump fits a 400 kVA supply but 150 kW does not, and it would use almost all output from up to about 300 kWp of solar.
- [Out-of-hours electricity in clinics and health centres](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/out-of-hours-electricity): Out-of-hours electricity on healthcare estates: where to look (health centres, outpatients, offices, education centres), setting clinic hours, finding it in HH data, common causes, and safe fixes under HTM 03-01 and HTM 04-01.
- [Hospital base load: what never switches off](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/base-load): Base load on healthcare sites: measured as the 5th percentile, base load by month and the 01:00 to 05:00 window; what makes it up in hospitals; theatre ventilation setback (132 to 286 MWh per theatre a year, NHS England 2026); safe ways to cut it.
- [Hospital supply capacity: kVA headroom for heat pumps](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/supply-capacity): Agreed supply capacity for hospitals: kW to kVA, headroom from a year of HH peaks with a margin, testing heat pumps over the heating months, CHP hiding demand, generator-backed supplies, and what to take to the DNO.
- [How to read a hospital electricity heatmap](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/reading-a-heatmap): Reading a half-hourly heatmap for hospitals and health centres: night rows as base load, the weekday band, summer cooling, and patterns such as failed ventilation setback, generator tests, CHP outages and missing data.
- [Proving NHS energy savings with half-hourly data](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/proving-savings): Proving an energy saving on a healthcare estate with HH data: matched periods, the right measure per change (setback, LED, VSDs, BMS schedules, solar, heat pumps), weather, analyser tools and formal M&V under IPMVP.
- [Glossary of hospital energy and HH data terms](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/glossary): Definitions: base load, closed-hours excess, kW, kWh, kVA, power factor, MPAN, profile class, agreed supply capacity, settlement, MHHS, DUoS, TNUoS, BSUoS, Renewables Obligation, CfD, Capacity Market, nuclear RAB, CCL, red/amber/green bands and more.
- [Guides for healthcare estates: energy and net zero](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/guides): Index of guides.
- [Hospital solar payback: what decides it](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/solar-payback): Solar payback on hospitals: share used on site (99.8% at 299 kWp in the example hospital), unit price, mounting, CHP, roof condition, business rates exemption, NHS versus private tax, and how to shorten payback.
- [Hospital solar: planning permission and grid connection](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/solar-planning-and-grid): Planning and grid connection for hospital solar: G99 types and timescales, export limits (cheap for 24-hour sites), permitted development in England since December 2023, listed buildings, helipad glint and glare, generators, PFI consent and a typical timeline.
- [Paying for solar on NHS and private hospital sites](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/paying-for-solar): Paying for hospital solar: capital purchase, grants (GBE £100m for NHS solar announced March 2025; PSDS not funded for new rounds beyond 2027/28), PPAs and their accounting, leases, business rates exemption in England, and tax for private hospitals.

## Sectors

- [Energy and net zero for independent hospitals](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/private-hospitals): Private and independent hospitals: ESOS Phase 4 (qualification 31 Dec 2026, notify by 5 Dec 2027), SECR, NHS supplier carbon reduction plans (all procurements since April 2024; 2027 standard for contracts of £5m a year or more), IHPN net zero by 2035, solar and efficiency.
- [Acute hospital electricity: HH data, capacity and solar](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/acute-hospitals): Acute hospitals: what normal half-hourly demand looks like, what to check first, how to set the hours, and the capacity and solar questions.
- [Community and mental health sites: energy and HH data](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/community-and-mental-health): Community and mental health sites: what normal half-hourly demand looks like, what to check first, how to set the hours, and the capacity and solar questions.
- [Health centres and clinics: electricity use and HH data](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/health-centres-and-clinics): Health centres, clinics and GP premises: what normal half-hourly demand looks like, what to check first, how to set the hours, and the capacity and solar questions.
- [Ambulance stations: electricity, EV charging and solar](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/ambulance-stations-and-fleet): Ambulance stations and fleet depots: what normal half-hourly demand looks like, what to check first, how to set the hours, and the capacity and solar questions.
- [Healthcare settings: what to look for in HH data](https://hospitalenergyinsights.co.uk/sectors): Index of healthcare settings pages.
